items.title: Meta completes $15B of senior-note issuance
items.summary: Meta’s November 5 SEC filing confirms completion that day of five senior-note tranches totaling $15 billion in principal. That total is the sum of the disclosed $3.25B, $3.25B, $4B, $1.75B and $2.75B issues. Coupons range from 5.850% to 7.500%, with maturities from 2031 to 2056. This is completed company-level financing by a major AI infrastructure buyer; the principal amount does not establish net cash proceeds, an AI-specific spending allocation or installed compute capacity.

sources.title: Meta Form 8-K, Item 8.01: completed USD senior-note offering

items.impact_reason: A substantial completed capital-market transaction changes the funding and obligations of a major compute owner. The filing does not establish an AI allocation or capacity conversion.
items.confidence: High for SEC-filed completion and terms; $15B is the arithmetic sum of the five disclosed principal amounts.
items.event_date_scope: Offering completion and filing date; the cover reports November 3 as the earliest event. Editorial review is November 6.

items.title: IREN reports $200M AI Cloud revenue as its >$4B run-rate target moves into 2027
items.summary: IREN’s November 5 release reports $200 million of AI Cloud revenue for the quarter ended September 30: $135 million of services and $65 million of leases. Its more-than-$4 billion annualized run-rate target moves from year-end 2026 to January 31, potentially the end of February, following a customer-requested change and supplier timing. Management calls that 0.3GW IT program fully funded, but its definition includes restricted cash, undrawn financing and contracted prepayments not yet received, with funding conditions. Operating run-rate revenue is about $1 billion. Neither operating ARR nor the future target is GAAP revenue; commissioning and customer acceptance govern the ramp.

sources.title: IREN Q1 FY27 results, financial summary and assumptions 1, 4 and 5

items.impact_reason: A major neocloud reports a larger AI business while moving a substantial contracted ramp into 2027. Mixed revenue streams and conditional funding require separate measures.
items.confidence: Company-reported results and timing; run-rate targets depend on pricing, utilization and delivery assumptions.
items.event_date_scope: Results announcement; quarterly revenue covers July–September 2026. Editorial review is November 6.
items.future_target: > $4B ARR targeted for January 31, 2027, potentially extending to February end.

items.title: Core Scientific reports $215.4M colocation revenue and 485MW billing capacity
items.summary: Core Scientific’s November 5 results report $215.4 million of third-quarter colocation revenue, compared with $136.7 million in Q2. The company was billing 485MW at September 30, up from 395MW at June 30. Its definition requires service to have commenced and customers to be actively billed; this is a customer billing metric, not measured electricity consumption or GPU utilization. Management says its first colocation agreement is nearing full delivery while construction under its second continues across five campuses. The results show a real revenue and service ramp, while undelivered contracted capacity remains future supply.

sources.title: Core Scientific Q3 2026 results, operating metrics and Term Library

items.impact_reason: Higher colocation revenue and billable capacity demonstrate a substantial hosting ramp. Billing power and future construction cannot establish tenant-owned GPU availability or utilization.
items.confidence: High for the company-reported financial and billing metrics; service and construction commentary is management-reported.
items.event_date_scope: Results publication; quarter-end billing observations are September 30 and June 30, 2026. Editorial review is November 6.

items.title: TeraWulf’s HPC lease revenue reaches $63M; 102MW operates while 336MW is being built
items.summary: TeraWulf’s November 6 results report $62.986 million of third-quarter HPC lease revenue, roughly 83% of $76.230 million total revenue. Lake Mariner had 102MW of revenue-generating critical IT capacity at September 30 and another 336MW under construction across CB-4 and CB-5. Phased CB-4 delivery and rent commencement remain expected in Q4; CB-5 is targeted to begin phased delivery in early 2027. The growing lease business remains distinct from the construction pipeline. The release also repeats the November 4 Justified credit-support and EPC agreements; those are the previously reported development, not another $19 billion lease or completed financing.

sources.title: TeraWulf Q3 2026 results, Lake Mariner milestones and income statement

items.impact_reason: HPC leases now account for most quarterly revenue, while a much larger construction pipeline still awaits delivery. This is a material regional hosting transition.
items.confidence: High for reported revenue and September operating/construction figures; future service dates remain targets.
items.event_date_scope: Results announcement; revenue and operating capacity describe the quarter ended September 30.
items.future_target: CB-4 phased delivery/rent in Q4 2026; CB-5 phased delivery beginning early 2027.

items.title: TeraWulf adds conditional Google backstop and Fluor construction contract at Justified
items.summary: TeraWulf’s November 4 filing describes Google credit support for certain Anthropic obligations under existing Justified leases in Kentucky. The backstop becomes effective for each lease when its final data hall starts. Following specified tenant defaults, Google can assume the lease and pay rent or, in certain circumstances, pay a termination fee that entitles it to an equity interest in the project subsidiary. The approximately $19 billion is existing lease commitments, not a new loan or another lease to add. A separate Fluor engineering, procurement and construction agreement covers three buildings; guaranteed maximum pricing is still being established. Phased service is expected from late 2027 through Q2 2028. These are financing and execution milestones, while debt funding and delivered capacity remain prospective.

sources.title: TeraWulf Form 8-K, Justified Credit Support Agreements, Items 1.01 and 8.01
TeraWulf announces Google credit support and definitive Fluor EPC agreement

items.impact_reason: Conditional credit support and a definitive construction agreement advance a substantial regional AI campus. Effectiveness conditions, debt funding and future delivery limit immediate supply implications.
items.confidence: High for the filed contractual terms; financing benefits and service milestones remain forward-looking.
items.event_date_scope: Agreements and announcement; the underlying Anthropic lease was announced July 6. Editorial review is November 5.
items.future_target: Phased ready-for-service completions expected from late 2027 through Q2 2028; no operating capacity established here.

items.title: Coherent’s datacenter and communications sales rise 79% to $1.95B
items.summary: Coherent’s November 4 results show $1.9517 billion of Datacenter & Communications revenue for the quarter ended September 30, compared with $1.0900 billion a year earlier. That is 79.1% growth calculated from its segment table. Company-wide revenue was $2.3703 billion, up about 50%. The expansion is a substantial commercial signal from an optical-component supplier serving AI infrastructure, but the segment also includes communications products and is not AI-only revenue. Sales dollars do not establish how much networking capacity is installed, utilized or available to AI users. The report supports strong supplier demand without resolving downstream construction and power constraints.

sources.title: Coherent first-quarter fiscal 2027 results, segment revenues in Table 5

items.impact_reason: Strong growth in a nearly $2B quarterly optical and communications segment is a substantial supply-chain development. Mixed end markets and absent deployment quantities limit broader capacity conclusions.
items.confidence: High for company-reported revenue; 79.1% segment growth is derived as (1,951.7 / 1,090.0 − 1) × 100.
items.event_date_scope: Results announcement; financial measurements cover the quarter ended September 30. Editorial review is November 5.

items.title: AMD’s data-center revenue nearly doubles to $8.55B as MI450 systems reach customers
items.summary: AMD’s November 3 earnings release reports $8.546 billion of Data Center revenue for the quarter ended September 26, up 97% year over year. AMD attributes growth to EPYC processors and the launch of Instinct MI450 GPUs, and says Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle are running workloads on the first Helios systems. This is evidence of commercial momentum for another large AI infrastructure supplier, but the segment includes CPUs and other products: it is not GPU-only sales or an installed-accelerator count. AMD’s approximately $17 billion fourth-quarter outlook is company-wide guidance, rather than a reported data-center result or a guarantee of future deliveries.

sources.title: AMD third-quarter 2026 financial results, segment table and current outlook

items.impact_reason: Nearly doubled quarterly sales and reported Helios workload deployments are substantial developments for the AI hardware segment. Product mix and deployment scale remain unspecified.
items.confidence: High for the company-reported financial results; customer workload deployments are AMD’s assertion, without disclosed system counts.
items.event_date_scope: Earnings announcement; results cover the quarter ended September 26. Editorial review is November 4.
items.future_target: Approximately $17B company-wide Q4 revenue, plus or minus 3%, is management guidance.

items.title: LandGate counts 819 US data-center announcements through October, above all of 2025
items.summary: LandGate’s November 4 report says 819 US data-center projects were announced in 2026 through October, exceeding its 764 for all of 2025. In its 6,561-project tracker, 3,045 are in development and 3,191 operating; 71% of the development pipeline is classified as hyperscale. The survey points to a large proposed buildout, while project counts do not measure megawatts, AI utilization or completed construction. LandGate identifies grid interconnection and local approvals as execution constraints. Its claim that capital has ceased to be the limiting factor is the research provider’s interpretation, not proof that every developer is funded. The tracked development pipeline must remain separate from operating supply.

items.impact_reason: A national tracker reports substantial announced expansion, with a development pipeline approaching the operating project count. Counts and approval exposure do not establish delivered compute capacity.

items.event_date_scope: Report publication. Announcement comparison covers January–October 2026 versus full-year 2025; the release does not specify an exact tracker snapshot day.

items.title: DigitalOcean reports roughly 10× quarterly inference-token growth and $376M AI customer ARR
items.summary: DigitalOcean’s November 3 results report $321 million of revenue for the quarter ended September 30, up 40% year over year, and $376 million of AI Customer ARR, up 288%. That ARR annualizes the quarter’s revenue from customers using AI/ML offerings and includes their other cloud services; it is not inference-only revenue. Management says Inference Engine token volume grew roughly tenfold from the prior quarter, without disclosing an absolute count. It also says 20 incremental megawatts have been secured for 2028. The results support accelerating demand at this provider, while the token ratio supplies no platform-wide daily total and the future megawatts are not operating capacity.

sources.title: DigitalOcean announces third-quarter 2026 financial results; metric definitions included

items.impact_reason: Rapid inference growth and a larger AI customer cohort are a substantial cloud-segment development. Unspecified absolute token volume and future capacity limit conclusions about global supply.
items.confidence: High for the company-reported results and metric definitions; the approximate token-growth ratio is management-reported.
items.event_date_scope: Results announcement; financial measurements cover the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
items.future_target: 20 incremental MW secured for 2028; service-start timing and comparable IT-load basis are not disclosed.

items.title: OpenAI launches grid-flexibility program, building on Georgia’s up-to-1GW agreement
items.summary: OpenAI announced Grid Protectors on November 2 to negotiate demand-reduction arrangements for future compute campuses. Its pilot is the planned Effingham County, Georgia campus, whose agreement includes up to 1,000MW of flexible demand response once operating. Georgia Power disclosed that commitment on July 22 under a 25-year agreement for a facility expected to need approximately 3,200MW. The new announcement extends that model into a national program; it does not announce a new 1GW block of generation or an operating campus. Local response amounts, speed and duration will vary, and further commitments remain to be finalized. Grid flexibility could affect how large AI loads secure utility service, but delivered curtailment has not been established.

sources.title: OpenAI introduces the Grid Protectors Program

items.impact_reason: An up-to-1GW flexibility agreement is a substantial regional grid-integration commitment and a proposed model for other campuses. The campus and wider rollout remain prospective.
items.confidence: High for the announced program and agreement terms, corroborated by the utility; actual operating performance remains unmeasured.
items.event_date_scope: National program announcement; the Georgia agreement was already publicly disclosed July 22. Editorial review dated November 3.
items.future_target: Effingham pilot once the planned campus operates; this announcement gives no operating date.

items.title: Marvell proposes $115B Lumentum acquisition to combine chip and optical connectivity
items.summary: Marvell and Lumentum announced on November 2 that Marvell would acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction with an implied enterprise value of $115 billion. Each Lumentum share would receive 4.500 Marvell shares. Combining Marvell’s interconnect and custom-silicon portfolio with Lumentum’s lasers, optical transceivers and optical switching could change how AI systems source connections between chips and data centers. That integration remains prospective: the companies expect closing in the first half of 2028, subject to both companies’ shareholder approvals, regulatory approvals and other conditions. The announced valuation is not cash investment in new compute capacity or evidence of measured performance gains.

sources.title: Marvell and Lumentum to Combine, Creating a Category Leader in AI Connectivity
Marvell Form 8-K, report dated November 1 and furnished November 2, 2026

items.impact_reason: A very large proposed combination of electrical and optical connectivity suppliers could reshape AI-system integration and sourcing across customers. The long closing horizon and required approvals limit immediate delivery implications.
items.confidence: High for announced terms, based on the joint primary release and Marvell’s 8-K; future integration benefits remain company expectations.
items.event_date_scope: Public announcement. Marvell’s 8-K cover identifies November 1 as the earliest event reported; do not conflate the announcement with signing or closing.
items.future_target: First half of calendar 2028, expected closing subject to conditions

items.title: Oracle completes $10B stock sale and $10B note issuance on November 4
items.summary: Oracle’s November 4 SEC filing confirms that its 86,206,897-share common-stock sale and $10 billion principal amount of senior notes closed that day. The shares were priced at $116, approximately $10 billion gross. The five note tranches mature from 2029 to 2046. This updates the November 2 pricing story under its original archive ID and date. Proceeds have broad corporate uses, including possible capital expenditure and debt repayment; the completed financing does not establish an AI-specific construction budget or delivered capacity.

items.title: Anthropic’s compute commitments carry different risks
items.summary: Anthropic’s November 2 amended S-1 describes minimum spending of $110 billion with AWS from May 2026 through April 2036 and $44.9 billion with Microsoft from November 2026 through June 2033, subject to specified exceptions. The Microsoft end date updates the earlier filing’s May 2033 date. SpaceX arrangements total up to $120.5 billion through 2029, but either party can cancel on 90 days’ notice after initial noncancelable periods ending in January and March 2027. Across purchase commitments and leases entered into as of and after September 30, Anthropic reports approximately $895.4 billion, largely for compute and infrastructure; $213.8 billion involves exercisable termination rights or conditions before commencement. These overlapping totals are not new deals to add together, supplier-recognized revenue or delivered capacity.

items.impact_reason: Material commitments across several major compute suppliers; cancellation rights affect revenue certainty without establishing delivered capacity.
items.confidence: High for the filed amounts and contract qualifications; future payments depend on the disclosed terms.

items.title: LG CNS reports completion of a 30MW-class AI data center in Jakarta
items.summary: LG CNS said on November 2 that it had completed a 30MW-class AI data center in Jakarta for KMG, a venture backed by Sinar Mas and Korea Investment Real Asset Management. The company says customers for its full capacity were secured before completion. This is a concrete regional construction milestone, while GPU deployment and utilization remain undisclosed. The first phase uses air cooling; liquid cooling is planned for later phases. A future expansion to 400MW of total incoming electrical capacity remains in design and must not be counted as completed capacity. The release does not establish a comparable IT-load figure or installed GPU count.

sources.title: LG CNS: first overseas AI data-center construction completed, 30MW-class facility in Indonesia (Korean)

items.impact_reason: A completed and reportedly customer-contracted facility adds a meaningful regional supply milestone. Its scale and undisclosed GPU/service ramp do not establish a global capacity shift.
items.confidence: High that LG CNS made this disclosure; capacity and customer claims are company-reported, not independently verified. IT-load scope and GPU availability remain unresolved.
items.event_date_scope: Completion announcement; exact physical completion and customer service-start dates are not established by the release.
items.future_target: Later-phase design envisages 400MW total incoming electrical capacity; no completion date stated
